Definition: from a primary μῖσος (hatred); to detest (especially to persecute); by extension, to love less:--hate(-ful).
BiblicalUsage: The word is to hate, and the New Testament uses it in both directions. Jesus quotes the old saying, love your neighbour and hate your enemy, and then overturns it; He says a disciple must hate his own life by comparison with Christ; and He warns that the world hated Him first, so it will hate His people too. John presses it further: whoever hates his brother is a murderer.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hatred is the test of love. We cannot claim to love God while hating our brother, and the only hatred Christ commands is the hatred of our own life when it competes with Him.
